title: Time visualizer and countdown
body:
I’ve been using Weel for several years and I love how it represents my schedule with a clock-like graph. The day and month views visualize when events occur during the day. I use the widgets to keep tabs on my day with a countdown of upcoming events and a visual reminder of the remaining time for current events. The standby mode widgets are helpful when docked on a desk or at night as a reminder of the upcoming day.  

Would love to see lockscreen widgets added.
author: Toasted Angle

title: Works well for time blindness
body: Seeing time blocks this way is very helpful. Still getting used to the app’s features yet when I use it , I feel more in control
author: ChilledWill

title: Great app
body: The data layout in the wheel, and global time zone support is very nice and very well designed. Looking forward to putting it through its paces! I appreciate that all data stays local. It would be fantastic if there was some way to add a return travel time.
author: Simianspaceman

title: Не доработано
body: Классное приложение! То что я хотела. Весь календарь и расписание дня на круге. Но, интерфейс неудобный. Добавлять событие интуитивно непонятно. Виджет глючит, иногда показывает заполненный полностью круг, хотя событий нет. Поправьте, пожалуйста
author: appplegreen

title: Paywall Slop
body: Good concept until you realize necessary features like “event colors” are locked behind a paywall… just manure it free with ads or figure out a way to sell a subscription without scummy tactics.
author: brock556

title: Why A Subscription?!?
body: The things that you’re offering like different colored events does not in any way warrant a subscription! I don’t care if it’s only 5 a month, this is one time purchase stuff at best. Nothing you’re offering requires constant maintenance on your end, like if you were to provide a cloud based service of your own. This app requires none of that from you, and so why do you ask us to pay you regularly??? Quit being greedy!
author: AlissUnknown

title: Best Calendar App
body: The Smartest visualization of your day’s activities/habits and meetings in a 24hr clock/circular format.  A refreshing take on your time, in a calendar & todo app in one hybrid. Worth a look for sure.
author: oliverlestrange

title: I really want this to work but I hate it.
body: The wheel format for the day is exactly what I want. But the only way to make this app work is to allow full access to my calendar and any event I put in Weel gets added to my actual calendar too. I share my calendar with my husband and I wanted a scheduling app that’s JUST FOR ME FOR MY OWN DAY. it won’t allow me to add any event that’s not tied to my calendar and I freaking hate that. If you don’t allow full access or any access to calendars, it won’t even let you add any event to your schedule. Those should be optional features. Good grief.
author: LaneTheLee

title: Maybe we need something different
body: I’ve been struggling to find anything that will help me orient myself to time. I have been using this for a few days, and I still have some ways to go in implementing it. However, for the first time I can see myself identifying lapses in a day between calendar events and logging what I have actually done. That evidence is helpful in understanding what does and does not work. I’m currently sitting at a restaurant and saw the dial post to 7pm. it helped me understand I have two more hours before the time I would typically want to crawl in bed and read a book (when I’m not working late nights bc dopamine surge). So, I was able to think.. how do I want to spend it? All of this to say, thanks for helping me feel a flash of hope. Would really love to connect with the developers to see how I can make this stick.
author: portiapreston

title: my favorite app
body: I honestly really love the weel app!! I take any opportunity to talk about this app to everyone I am friends with. I have used weel every single day of my undergrad experience, but I was really worried about being able to afford it now that I have started graduate school. The team was so kind and sent me a discount code for the year that will seriously make such a big difference!!!! I am eternally grateful and I love this app even more now. Sometimes there are some little bugs and glitches but I love this app too much to complain. 💗
author: itsyazzzmin

title: Great concept, poorly executed
body: I accepted the free trial to have access to the “premium” features, which are really just basic features like repeating events, so you’re forced to subscribe, and immediately realized this app isn’t worth a dime. Upon setting up my first event, work, I noticed that “travel time” is only accounted for at the beginning of the event. Apparently at the end of the event you just teleport home. Second thing I noticed is that there’s no option for an event to repeat a couple times a week, it’s either every weekday or you’re creating a new event for each day. These two issues right away signaled that this is just a money grab and isn’t thought through in the least bit. It’s 2026, apps aren’t THAT hard to create these days. Basic functionality shouldn’t be this bad.
author: CrypticalError

title: Please do better

Yes it plays nice with other apps like tick tick but there's such a long route to get there the apps "synced".  I love the wheel but why cant have that on our apple watch as well? I fr think this app has potential for someone like me who has ADHD but it's not worth a $149 life time subscription. A bit bold of a price for something that seems very half baked.

author: V11perQueen

title: LOVE THIS APP!
body:
This app changed my life!!! It’s the best calendar I’ve had to organize my life. I love how the face is 24 hours and I can easily add appointments. I can also easily check what time it will be in my time zone when friends from abroad ask to schedule appointments. I love how I can add transit options (walking, biking or driving) so my calendar tells me exactly when to leave. I’m a fan of how many color options I can use for different appointments and how easy it was (and still is) to sync my other calendars with this one once I downloaded it. My wife has the same app and we can easily sync our appointments. 

Most of the complaints about this app have been bug fixes that are now fixed. I’m happy to pay for an app that doesn’t sell my information or I am not the product they are selling. Thank you for creating such a great app that helps to keep my life organized!

author: Oddomission

title: This is the app I have been searching for
body:
Update: I am happy to report that I have continued using the app to great effect. The glitch I reported in my earlier review was the result of user error. As I’ve become more comfortable using the app, I realized I simply did not notice that you sometimes need to scroll up/down to see your text when writing notes. When opening notes, they don’t always generate where you left off. 
However, I have a fresh request. I have created a recurring daily “diary” task to track my progress. After a week of work, I realized that the edits I made erased my earlier notations (at times, I see an option to select “Save for this event” v. “save for future events,” but this does not appear reliably and it shows up on the bottom of my screen in a place where it is very difficult for me to click on it (I can only see half a line of the text at a time, if at all. I need to scroll up/down to choose and option and because this appears at the bottom of the screen, my IPad thinks I intend to close the app instead.)
I would love to see a diary option added to the interface so that I no longer need to create an event for it every day. I would also love for this/any notes to have a search function that will allow me to easily pull up when I had a meeting with a specific person or when we discussed a specific event. 

All-in-all, this is the best app I have found to assist with my complex executive functioning deficits. As an autistic person working in a professional administrative position, this app is a life saver. I am intensely grateful for the work that was put into this.

I have been looking for an app that combined Reminders (with check lists), a visual clock like the Wakka app, and Notes into one. I usually use all my tech in dark mood. However, I cannot see the text when writing notes for the day in dark mode. If this is not simply a glitch, then I feel they should not charge a subscription fee to use Light mode. Please update this note taking feature.

title: Visually interesting, but missing a few things
body:
I love the design of this app so much I ended up buying a subscription after 3 days! Being able to visualize my time this way has made a world of difference, especially the way you can layer calendars within rings!

The biggest missing feature for me is no ability to include travel time, which is often my biggest hitch. It wouldn’t have to be Google Maps perfect (though I can only imagine what a game changer this app is for a bus schedule!!), but even the ability to include a rough average would be a huge boon to your user base!

I definitely love the widgets and I can see myself keeping this app just for that, regardless of whether the above suggestions are implemented. I plan to also use this to help plan out my trips into town, so I can better see my bus/timing options

author: kmb462889

title: Little kinks make it difficult
body:
I really like this app but I wish it had a few more features. 

I wish there was an option for weekdays or weekends so I can more easily set up routines. Maybe the reoccurring option would allow you to pick the days they reoccur? Like a Tues, Thurs, reoccurring event is a little challenging to add. Plus you can’t copy/paste events. For someone who has the “out of sight/out of mind” ADHD, this tool becomes more challenging than helpful in this area. I also wish there was an “all day busy” feature that I could see on the pi chart so I could see that I can’t schedule anything on a day. I tried doing something similar by doing 12am-11:55pm but it leaves a really annoying little sliver that I can’t stop staring at. Also, I need to be able to schedule multiple reminders (like 10) for some things. So more opportunity for reminders are helpful. 

I know this is being advertised for people with ADHD but the app still feels very neurotypical to be honest.

author: daviddavini

title: Crashes before I can even set it up
body:
It seems like it’d be a cool app, but it’s hard to say cuz it crashes the second after I set up the first scheduled event (I couldn’t find a way to get into the app without setting one up.) When setting up the first event, I was unable to see what I was typing in the “location” box cuz the keyboard covers it completely and doesn’t allow you to scroll down so it’s visible above the keyboard. Then after I had set up all the features of it I wanted, it wouldn’t allow me to continue until I added it to one of my ical calendars i had allowed it to sync with (family, personal, medical, etc.) but the first time, it only gave me 2 choices, both of which were “read-only” calendars I had imported from my kid’s school and scout troop. Except they were both greyed-out and unable to be chosen, and you can’t move on without choosing one. I forget how I eventually got around that (it wasn’t ideal but I planned to try to go back and edit it once it had been created) but regardless, within a second of creating the event, the app crashed and every time I tried to reopen it, it would crash again.

Ok, fine. I’ve already agreed to the 7-day free trial, so I uninstalled and redownloaded it, went through the whole process again. This time I created the event with a different ring, and I’m not sure why that made a difference (since I hadn’t been able to explore the app at all cuz you can’t do that until you create an event) but this time I still had to add the event to one of my iCal synced calendars. It was only giving me 2 options out of about 6 or 7, but I just picked one, again planning to update/edit it after it was created, but then it just kept crashing again.

At this point, as I said, I have already begun the 7-day trial, and even if these other issues somehow got resolved, I’d be curious to see how that could get fixed as well so I could actually have a fair chance to try it before having to pay a subscription to even see if I like it. For the time being, I’ll be canceling the subscription so I don’t forget to cancel it before it autocharges me the monthly fee in 6 days. 

I’d be happy to amend this review if/when these issues are resolved and I’m able to give an actual review of the app itself instead of just reviewing my inability to even test drive it.
